#1347. Revealed: Just two Man United stars are selected in combined XI with Liverpool by stats boffins as Andoni Iraola's defence dominates... but is the Liverpool boss missing a hidden gem?

Published: 01:43 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 01:45 EST, 22 November 2026

All eyes will be on Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino when they take on Liverpool at Anfield this afternoon.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has freshened up the squad since joining in the summer, including the £123million purchase of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while blending in young emerging talent. They have made a solid start across all four competitions, knocking Chelsea out of the League Cup on penalties, and they currently sit in fourth place in the Premier League.

United have had a dire start to the season, with only one win in 10 games leading to the axeing of head coach Michael Carrick. Will his replacement be able to save the season and galvanise a group of talented but dispirited players?

So, who from United’s struggling side have done enough to break into Sofascore's combined XI based on their performances throughout the 2026-27 season so far?

Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday

United currently sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season

Between the sticks is Liverpool’s No 1, who since signing for a record fee in 2018, has established himself as one of the best shot-stoppers in the world.

Rated for his positioning, distribution and consistency, Alisson has an impressive record, especially in one-on-one situations.

The 34-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper has kept four clean sheets in 10 league appearances this season, averaging 2.5 saves per game. He has conceded 10 goals, including a brutal 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield last month.

Alisson was poor in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce but responded with a fine display in the Reds' 3-1 win over Crystal Palace when back in league action days later.

At right back is Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona this season, and there are already cries from Liverpool fans to sign him permanently.

The 27-year-old is a natural centre back, but he has done wonders to ease Liverpool’s problems in the right-back position. Jeremie Frimpong started the season in that position but the Liverpool backline were far too exposed. Araujo has helped Liverpool tighten up defensively.

The Uruguayan defender has featured in all of Liverpool’s league matches so far this season, with his defensive actions helping him contribute inside his own penalty box. He has averaged six clearances per game and has won 30 aerial duels so far this season, behind only Virgil van Dijk in the Liverpool squad.

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona

Jeremy Jacquet is a young player to watch this season after joining Liverpool this summer.

The 21-year-old has a 95 per cent accurate pass rate, including long balls. He had a standout performance against Fulham early on in the season, winning five aerial duels, five recoveries and making a clearance off the line to keep his team in the game.

Despite playing in France's second division just two seasons ago, Jacquet has fitted seamlessly into Iraola's style of play at Liverpool and there are suggestions he is an upgrade on the man he replaced, fellow France international Ibrahima Konate.

Centre back - Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool)

It is no surprise that Liverpool and Netherlands team captain Virgil van Dijk makes it into the XI.

Known for his strength, leadership, speed and aerial ability, he is the only defender to win the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award, and finished runner-up for both the Ballon d'Or and Best FIFA Men's Player in 2019.

This season, he has shown his aerial ability with 3.8 duels won in the air (79 per cent) per game and 4.8 total duels won per game.

The team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a big decision to make.

Is Iraola missing a hidden gem? Tsimikas is very much understudy to Milos Kerkez after acting as a reliable deputy to Andy Robertson.

But across all competitions this season he is statistically rated higher than the man who's ahead of him in the pecking order. Kerkez is rated at 6.67 – so it is tight.

Nicknamed 'Greek Scouser' by Reds fans, Tsimikas has only started five games but has produced three assists with 1.78 key passes and 1.56 accurate crosses.

Manchester United, on the other hand, have struggled to fill this position. They were unable to recruit in the summer, and now rely on Luke Shaw – who has been sidelined with a muscular issue since limping off during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur in October – and are adapting with makeshift alternatives.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace

Centre midfield – Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool)

Versatile vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai signed a new five-year contract with Liverpool this summer, and has proven his worth after scoring a stoppage-time penalty to level the score in their first game of the season against Newcastle.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating big chances.

It is a testament to his creative ability, including registering four big chances and one assist in the Premier League this season, that he makes the XI despite being sidelined with a hamstring injury for three games.

However, the Hungary midfielder has received backlash from fans for playing 90 minutes for his country in a 2-0 win against Georgia in the UEFA Nations League despite early withdrawal against Palace, and injury concerns remain ahead of this afternoon's clash.

Centre midfield – Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United)

Only one of two Manchester United players in this line-up, Kobbie Mainoo deserves recognition for his creative efforts this season, which have earned him the second highest Sofascore rating in this XI.

The 21-year-old England midfielder is known for his high pressing and long balls to create chances up the pitch. He has also registered four shots from outside the box.

He has been through some turbulent times at Old Trafford but Michael Carrick turned to him regularly this season.

A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend

Centre midfield – Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool)

After his public revelation that he nearly left Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister has been in form and pulling the strings in midfield and played an important role in Liverpool's season so far.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Right forward – Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Portugal forward was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year last season, but he has divided United fans this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

In the 1-1 draw against Spurs at Old Trafford, the skipper did not record his first successful pass until the 23rd minute, and he missed a big chance against Chelsea.

He has bagged four goals and two assists in the Premier League so far, but this is largely owing to his hat-trick against Ipswich, which earned him a perfect 10 Sofascore rating.

United fans will hope he can get back to his old ways under Pochettino.

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again

Centre-forward – Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Liverpool’s star striker, transferred for a British record-breaking fee of £125million last summer, has scored eight goals in 14 games this season, showing just how clinical he can be.

Reds fans are finally seeing the form that earned him the big-money move from Newcastle.

Isak edges out United's Bryan Mbeumo to lead the line in this team. He has a 55.6 per cent big chance conversion, scoring a goal every 113 minutes.

The Dutchman is establishing himself as Liverpool's go-to wideman among Iraola's plethora of options. His rapid pace and direct approach proves a massive threat.

This season his end product has improved, notching three goals and supplying six assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

He is proving to be a reliable outlet while summer signings Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz continue to settle into life in England.

His stunning long-range strike to equalise against Newcastle United shows just how clinical he can be in front of goal.

He averages 1.9 key passes and one big chance per game, which lands him a spot in this XI.

#1346. Kings of the jungle? This early human had surprising survival skills that rivalled ours

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL

Homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives. The big-brained, tool-wielding species emerged two million years ago in Africa and expanded across Eurasia, before vanishing around 100,000 years ago in Java, Indonesia.

Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts

Did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts

Researchers have now added another feather to the hominin’s cap. A pair of studies analysing fossil teeth1,2, which were published in Nature on 18 November, suggest that H. erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago.

Researchers had thought that H. erectus was limited to savannahs and open woodlands, says Kira Westaway, a geochronologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, and a co-author of both studies.

“Never, ever have we seen them in rainforests,” she adds. “This is a really big deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”

The earliest H. erectus fossils, from eastern Africa, are 1.9 million years old. But the svelte, upright-walking and running hominins wasted little time, reaching western Asia and present-day China some 200,000 years later and modern Java, using land bridges, not long after. The last-known H. erectus remains, from central Java, date to roughly 110,000 years ago3.

Limestone caves in Guangxi province, southern China, contained more than 10,000 fossil teeth.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University)

While looking for fossils from a three-metre-tall great ape called Gigantopithecus, Westaway and her colleagues identified a pair of limestone caves in Guangxi province in southern China. There, they discovered more than 10,000 fossil teeth from animals such as orangutans (Pongo spp.), monkeys and wild boar (Sus spp.), as well as 9 from hominins. The researchers estimate that the hominins lived between 184,000 and 324,000 years ago, according to dating of both fossils and the surrounding sediments using various methods.

Eight of the hominin teeth resembled those of H. erectus in their shape, a designation that was confirmed by analysing the sequences of proteins preserved in the dental enamel of four specimens, says co-author Frido Welker, a molecular palaeoanthropologist at the University of Copenhagen.

The tooth enamel was analysed and its proteins sequenced.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University)

The ninth lacked the shape and protein signature of H. erectus teeth, says Welker, and it also didn’t resemble those of H. sapiens or Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis). Denisovans — enigmatic ancient humans first discovered in southern Siberia and now linked to diverse fossils from China and elsewhere in Asia — are a possibility, but the evidence is circumstantial, says Welker. “Every label we put on that ninth tooth is a little bit of speculation.”

The multitude of animal teeth was probably accumulated by a scavenger such as a porcupine. The presence of fossils from species such as muntjac deer (Muntiacus muntjac), leopards and orangutans hints at a rainforest environment.

#1345. Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

An extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

We could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

We wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

The tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

But the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are currently in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

#1344. Ten-Man Blues Undone At Brentford

Everton’s return to Premier League action proved a forgettable one as a 17-minute first-half spell ultimately condemned them to a 4-0 defeat at Brentford.

Looking to extend their three-match unbeaten run built before the recent international break, the Blues struggled to get going at the Gtech Stadium – before rotten luck left them with a mountain to climb.

On 23 minutes, Keane Lewis-Potter’s run into the area was picked out by Jaidon Anthony as his finish took a horrible deflection off Jarrad Branthwaite to beat Jordan Pickford.

Worse misfortune struck Everton two minutes later as Lewis-Potter’s shot was blocked by James Tarkowski, fell straight back into the path of the same Brentford player whose rebound was destined to be kept out again, only to hit Thierno Barry and wrong-foot Pickford.

The Toffees’ hopes of mounting a comeback were then all but ended five minutes before the interval when Tarkowski was penalised for a sliding tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk.

Initially slow to award the free-kick, referee Craig Pawson eventually showed the Blues captain a yellow card – only to be called over by VAR and soon change his decision to red for violent conduct.

Left to battle on with 10 men, Everton had a sniff of a comeback with seconds left of the first half when fine work from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall ended with the No.8 chipping in a cross that Barry did well to nod into the bottom right-hand corner, only for keeper Caoimhin Kelleher to somehow claw the ball away.

Jack Grealish came on for the start of the second half and soon made an impact with a teasing centre across the six-yard box that just evaded Barry.

But any hopes of an unlikely fightback were ended on 67 minutes as Vitaly Janelt fired a 25-yard strike into the top right-hand corner.

And a miserable night was summed up in the dying moments when Damsgaard's corner found its way to substitute Fabio Carvalho to tap over the line from a yard out.

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

Pep Guardiola, wearing a flat cap, has taken his seat in the Manchester City directors’ box, directly behind chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana. It is of course his first game back at the club after quitting as manager in the summer. It is also a declared show of solidarity after the guilty verdict.

It’s a special night against the best team in Europe, I hope it’s a special game. Pep is here but was not at the training ground. I have not spoken with him.

I said yesterday you need a complete performance, top on and off the ball to beat them. We will create some chances and concede some chances but you have to find the complete balance.

Under normal circumstances there would be a high level of anticipation around this game, even though it is the eighth time in 11 seasons that City and PSG have faced each other in the Champions League. But given the backdrop of City guilty verdict and it being the first home fixture since that announcement it is even more fascinating. There will also be, of course, Pep Guardiola back “in his house”, as his successor, Enzo Maresca. put it. The atmosphere will be interesting.

If the verdicts are upheld, of course, it wasn’t their penthouse and it wasn’t their caviar.

We got to live in a penthouse and eat caviar for 15 years and if we have to go back to a semi in the suburbs, well, fine.

When Manchester City endured their first major sanction over financial fair play in 2014, the biggest club accused alongside them that summer were Paris St-Germain, another Champions League arriviste who had been raised from mediocrity to the elite by some frantic spending from a Middle East fossil fuel dynasty.

Then, 12 years ago, both sides bitterly opposed the Uefa sanctions imposed on them – although they eventually agreed to the terms. Now, they face one another in Manchester with PSG aiming for a third consecutive Champions League title, and City fighting for their lives in the face of an overwhelming guilty verdict for nine years of Premier League rule-breaking.

Both clubs are transformed from the entities that their current owners acquired. While PSG now find themselves at the centre of the new order in European football, City are once again on the outside.

Whatever the outcome of this process, I won’t forget the connection and relationships I had here. It will never be erased.

Good evening, and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Manchester City and Paris St-Germain, champions in 2025 and 2026 and favourites to become only the fourth club, after Real Madrid (who have done it twice), Ajax and Bayern Munich to win a hat-trick of European Cups.

After Manchester City’s conviction by an independent commission on 114 charges of financial malpractice in contravention of Premier League rules, finding the right tone to use to cover their matches during their appeal is difficult. While they are in limbo, the rest of English football is in purgatory and although Gary Neville, the Pope of Pilsworth, in unsurprisingly hyperbolic fashion has said he would prefer not to cover City’s games in future, that is not an indulgence a serious news organisation would countenance. They have to be covered and the issues addressed.

Having said that, in this format of a rolling report on the old minute-by-minute template, I think we have to cover the controversy and its implications in the whole during the build-up and keep an eye on reaction and references to it during the run of play. But I don’t think it would serve anyone to take the stance during the live coverage that anything that is happening on the field is unimportant, redundant and ultimately void because of the guilty verdicts, and hence adopt a flippant tone. I propose once the match starts to treat it as a match while not ignoring the context.

Right, let’s get stuck into the Gulf State sovereign wealth fund derby… sorry, imposible to resist.

PSG have made a slow start to their Ligue 1 campaign, their worst since Luis Enrique’s first season in charge. Starting with two draws and a defeat, they have rallied with three successive victories to climb up to sixth as the head coach, as he tends to do in the league, rotates his midfielders and forwards like crazy, to whose ranks he has added the World Cup-winner Ferran Torres. The summer signing scored a hat-trick in his Champions League debut for the club, a 6-1 mauling of Slovan Bratislava.

City, too, started their European campaign with a win, Erling Haaland scoring both goals in the 2-0 victory over Porto at the Dragao and you won’t need me to remind you that they have won all six of their Premier League games to lead Arsenal by three points at the top of the table.

#1342. Bruno Fernandes reveals contract negotiations with Manchester United have stalled after he rejected a new deal in the summer

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed new deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but new manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United

'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

'And I've always said the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club says "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a new contract so I think that from their side shows that they want me to stay.

'As I said there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'

The club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a big-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

United currently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'

His post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he said. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference

'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

#1339. The next Lamine Yamal? Why not? Roberto De Zerbi sets high bar for Luca Williams-Barnett after 18-year-old thrilled Tottenham fans in win over Ipswich, writes MATT BARLOW

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026

Luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'

Asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

You make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

There has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

Spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

#1338. Pierre Sage’s Lyon return ends in disappointment for Crystal Palace

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” said Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

“I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

“When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”

The veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

Palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

Brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

#1336. Co-owner Brittany Mahomes leads wild celebrations as Kansas City Current wins NWSL title

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was announced as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

#1335. Microbiome home tests are taking off. Can they be trusted?

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Amber Dance is a freelance science writer near Los Angeles, California.

A mix of microorganisms from a human faecal sample, imaged using a scanning electron microscope. Credit: Steve Gschmeissner/Science Photo Library

First, the good news: I have 133 microbial species living in my gut. That’s a collection that ranks as ‘excellent’ according to NirvanaBiome, the company in Germantown, Maryland, that analysed my stool sample. The firm based its rating on the overall diversity of my gut’s residents plus my levels of specific beneficial and undesirable species.

Revealed: how this common gut microbe protects against heart disease

Revealed: how this common gut microbe protects against heart disease

But then came a second, less promising assessment: Viome in Bellevue, Washington, identified only 61 kinds of active microorganism in my gut and suggested that some of them were not performing optimally. Viome recommended dietary changes and offered customized supplements to improve my health.

I was intrigued by the results, but also flummoxed by the different messages. That’s not an uncommon response, says microbiologist Rob Knight, director of the Center for Microbiome Innovation at the University of California, San Diego. When scientists tested a handful of microbiome testing kits alongside one another in formal studies, they found wide discrepancies in the results. These differences make it hard to understand or really trust the findings from any given provider, says Diane Hoffmann, director of the Law and Health Care programme at the University of Maryland in Baltimore, who co-authored one of those studies.

The companies stand by their products. “Of course there’s variability,” says Kelly Moffat, chief operations officer for Cmbio in Germantown, which does the laboratory work and genetic sequencing for NirvanaBiome. “There has to be because this is complex testing.”

Momo Vuyisich, chief science officer at Viome’s lab in Bothwell, Washington, also says he was unsurprised by the degree of variation found by formal studies. Labs use different methods to extract, sequence and analyse microbial genetic material. Viome, for example, sequences RNA rather than DNA, allowing it to uncover microbial gene activity, rather than only the presence of genes. Vuyisich argues that this is more relevant to human health. And he says that although every method will have biases, as long as a consumer sticks with the same provider, it should produce results that are comparable over time.

Interest in these kinds of test is booming. “There’s so much public enthusiasm and excitement about the microbiome,” says Knight. Some customers are simply curious about the microscopic beings that live inside them and potentially affect their health; others have health conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome and hope that their gut microbes will reveal the underlying cause or a path to better health.

Although people can order the tests and follow their recommendations without the help of a medical professional, some people are bringing the findings to their physicians. “I groan when I see someone come in with a microbiome test,” says Fergus Shanahan, a gastroenterologist and immunologist at University College Cork in Ireland, who has spent much of his career studying the microbiome. For someone struggling with gut health, a consumer microbiome profile isn’t usually specific enough to help. And if there’s a concern about an infection, such as Clostridioides difficile, it’s more straightforward to test for known pathogens than to assess the entire microbial community.

The tantalizing links between gut microbes and the brain

The tantalizing links between gut microbes and the brain

Microbiologists and gasteroenterologists who spoke to Nature generally agreed that microbiome testing has the potential to both reflect and promote health, but many said that the science isn’t yet mature enough to support microbiome testing for most consumers. In their view, the limited clinical usefulness of today’s consumer tests can make them poor value for money (costing around US$100–300). The specialists warn that acting on advice that doesn’t come from clinicians could lead customers to adopt unnecessarily restrictive diets or delay appropriate medical assessment. Critics say that consumer microbiome testing needs more regulatory scrutiny and oversight.

“This is an industry that’s running wild,” says genomicist Jacques Ravel, director of the Center for Advanced Microbiome Research and Innovation at the University of Maryland School of Medicine in Baltimore and a co-author on one of the studies that tested several providers. With regards to testing methods, he says, “there’s no standard”.

Moffat says, “I think the jury’s out on exactly what it is that we can actionably do today based on this data.” But she says that microbiome profiles, combined with other testing such as gut metabolomics, could yield interesting and useful health information.

The gut microbiome has emerged as an incredible correlate of overall health. From immune-system function to metabolism, skin disorders and mental health, study after study has found links between a person’s well-being and the trillions of microbes that live in their digestive tract. The premise of a head count of these species and assessment of their actions, to monitor and improve gut health in a personalized way, certainly sounds appealing. Viome’s website, for example, promises: “No more trial and error … Follow a plan built precisely for you.”

Companies can identify species and, on the basis of those lists, infer what the microbes are probably doing, such as manufacturing metabolites or inciting inflammation. But running even the simplest microbiome testing is expensive, says Alessandra Cervino, research director at PiLeJe, a science-based food-supplement company in Paris. She says her microbiome testing company, Luxia Scientific, closed in 2024 for financial reasons.

Some microbiome testing firms recommend fermented foods, such as kombucha, for gut health.Credit: Deb Lindsey for The Washington Post via Getty

Many testing companies also offer lifestyle and nutritional advice or sell supplements. For example, Viome analysed diverse functions performed by the microbes in my gut, such as digestive efficiency, gas production and serotonin manufacture. I then received a detailed eating plan — which told me to eschew broccoli and load up on pecans, among other suggestions — along with an offer for precision supplements and probiotics with a price tag of more than $150 a month. Although it’s hard to change the composition of microbes in one’s gut, alterations in diet or even simply ageing can shift their activities, says Vuyisich. The company recommends re-testing every four to six months to check for shifts and update the plan.

He points to 19 peer-reviewed publications by Viome as evidence of the company’s rigour (see go.nature.com/4actdhq). For example, the firm’s analysis for consumers is supported, in part, by published data on how gut microbes influence individuals’ responses to glucose in various foods, based on 550 people in the United States who collectively ate more than 30,000 meals while wearing glucose monitors1. The company validated those findings in a further cohort in Japan, Vuyisich says, but those data are not published.

Microbiome tests are not created equal, says Tim Spector, a physician-scientist at King’s College London and co-founder of London-based ZOE, which offers microbiome testing and a supplement in addition to a gut-health app that I’ve been playing with. ZOE’s products, Spector says, are backed by research on thousands of people. “There definitely are some not-so-good players out there that give this field a bad name,” he says. “It’s not easy to do this well.”

There are also several ways to do microbe testing; companies take varying approaches that yield disparate results, as at least two studies have shown. Scientists at the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in Gaithersburg, Maryland, shipped homogenized stool samples from one person to seven companies2. NIST’s remit is researching and applying standards for measurement. This experiment was a step towards understanding the diversity of testing options out there, says one of the study authors, NIST microbiologist Stephanie Servetas, who is based in Sheridan, Wyoming. The researchers didn’t name the companies in their report because they wanted to focus attention on the comparison between tests rather than perceived accuracy of any individual provider.

The result: “Companies produce strikingly different results,” says co-author Scott Jackson, a molecular geneticist who used to direct the NIST microbiology program and is now a consultant in Saint Michaels, Maryland. “They couldn’t even agree on what’s healthy and unhealthy,” Jackson says. The microbe lists ranged from 34 to 906 identified genera; only 3 of which showed up in all reports. In fact, the results were as varied from company to company as they would be for different people, despite all tests being done on samples from the same individual.

A European and Canadian team obtained similar outcomes when they sent homogenized samples from one person’s stool to six companies, also anonymized. Three companies rated the microbial diversity as “excellent” or “good”; two called it “average”; one said it was “unfavourable”3. The results were so variable, that at least some of them must be lacking in validation or standardization, says co-author Céline Druart, executive director of the Pharmabiotic Research Institute (PRI) in Brussels, a non-profit organization specializing in regulation of microbiome innovations. “It’s very difficult to make a conclusion,” she says.

How gut bacteria could boost cancer treatments

How gut bacteria could boost cancer treatments

This broad divergence in results is not surprising, says Jack Gilbert, director of the Microbiome and Metagenomics Center at the University of California, San Diego. The variation starts at sampling: scoop a bit of faecal matter into a tube, stab it with a coring device or swipe the sampler across some used toilet paper; ship it off as-is, or in some kind of preservative (as both Viome’s and NirvanaBiome’s kits asked me to). Each option could influence the balance of the microbes that are collected and what survives to be sequenced.

In the lab, Servetas says the method by which the researchers extract genetic material from a sample is a big source of divergence. Gentler protocols will bias a sample towards microbes that are easy to crack open, whereas harsher methods will capture a higher share of species with tougher exteriors.

After sequencing, another major source of difference, says Knight, is the bioinformatics pipeline that labs use. What length or number of genetic sequences is required to consider a microbe present? What list of sequences and microbes are they using as a reference? “All bets are off when you then computationally analyse it with your favourite method,” says Knight.

Would companies support having standards to validate their tests? “We are really big advocates on really having a standard here,” says Kimberley Sukhum, chief science officer at Tiny Health in Austin, Texas, which offers gut microbiome tests as well as vaginal microbiome tests.

But it’s hard to set those standards, in part because there is no known ‘ground truth’ for a natural microbial sample. Compare that with, say, a blood-glucose test; a lab can get a known value from a standard sample either right or wrong. But the microbiome, in its glorious complexity, does not allow for such simple validation. NIST has used mixed human donor samples to develop a standard4. And Tiny Health has experimented with generating a reference for benchmarking from synthetic communities. It was built from individual microbial species rather than sampled from faeces5. But neither of those standards is exactly like the microbiome of an individual person.

Even if labs could assess a microbiome perfectly, they’d still have a problem: there’s no defined healthy microbiome like there is one range of healthy blood-glucose levels. Each person’s microbiome is unique, like a fingerprint. There are infinitely many ways to have a healthy microbiome, and infinitely many ways to have an unhealthy one, says Shanahan; it’s not entirely clear how to draw a line between the two.

How gut microbes could drive brain disorders

How gut microbes could drive brain disorders

Companies must compare customer microbiomes with some standard of health, but these vary too. They might be based on past customers or large, public databases. But microbiomes differ considerably depending on factors such as ethnicity, sex, age, recent antibiotic use or even whether someone was born by caesarean section.

#1333. Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury

This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

Alonso is speedily shifting perceptions of this previously underperforming bunch, the Stamford Bridge culture on and off the pitch already unrecognisable from a few months ago.

It was Chelsea’s trip to Everton last season which facilitated the endgame of Liam Rosenior’s short, but generally hideous reign.

For those who tried to banish memories, it was a darkly comical period when Chelsea’s players were paying their respect to stationary footballs, seemingly finding new ways to stand in front of travelling fans to apologise for meek and rancid performances.

How different the scenes after Pedro Neto’s double on Merseyside – a success built on those old-fashioned and too often underestimated qualities of character and application before the artists had the final say. These are the wins that build connections and trust between players and supporters, especially during the getting-to-know-you period of a managerial tenure. While neutrals mutter about a generally disappointing spectacle, the players and supporters return home clutching three points believing they have fought together in the trenches.

Neto fires past Pickford to double Chelsea's lead! 🔥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/SOJeBP5mq0

It cannot be overlooked how this win owed a debt to the erratic refereeing of Paul Tierney, especially the amnesty he offered to Morgan Rogers on the stroke of half-time.

Already booked, Rogers was fortunate not to receive a second caution for a lunge on James Garner which took the man after the ball. A replica challenge by Everton’s Harrison Armstrong had warranted a yellow card in Tierney’s world just 21 minutes earlier.

The home team’s argument that this was a potential game changer was supported when the England midfielder was inevitably involved in the move which led to Neto breaking through 44 seconds into the second half – a lead Chelsea never looked like surrendering as Everton’s attacking limitations were exposed.

Chelsea break the deadlock inside a minute of the second half! ⚡ Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/E63rtGQnbv

That should not disguise how this is a different Chelsea, contrasting not just with the characterless and rudderless team of last season, but also the defensively flawed version that began this one. Mike Penders deputised for the stricken Martínez – conscious but taken to hospital as a precaution – and was well-protected.

As much as Alonso’s artistry as a midfield maestro is presumed to define him as a coach, one cannot help but believe there are many who underestimate him as a football student. He was never going to return to England clinging to one idea given his previous Premier League experience, and he intuitively knew an away game at Everton was one for foot soldiers.

He signed Jordan Henderson for such a task. Just like his manager, the former Liverpool captain was primed for enemy territory.

Alonso’s anticipation of a fixture in which a battle had to be fought before there was an outbreak of football proved correct, aided by the fussy and generally terrible first-half officiating of Tierney.

Bizarrely, Alonso had as much cause to curse Tierney for the first of several contentious decisions, booking Armstrong for an aggressive but ultimately fair lunging challenge on Josh Acheampong. That enraged the home supporters to inspire Everton to their most dangerous spell, Thierno Barry coming closest to troubling Martínez before half-time.

Although Moisés Caicedo was denied a goal-of-the-season contender when a vicious 20-yard volley struck the crossbar, the scrappy, stop-start flavour of the occasion initially suited the hosts.

Caicedo rattles the woodwork with a stunning effort! 💥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/CSIM9ogtSp

Rogers’s reprieve changed all that. Inexplicably inconsistent as Tierney was, Chelsea exhibited a steel which thrilled Alonso as much as those games when Cole Palmer, Rogers and João Pedro are in full flow.

“They didn’t score, but did a fantastic job for the team,” Alonso pointedly said of his attackers.

Alonso’s name has not echoed so loudly across the Mersey since he played a few miles down the road from Everton’s new home. After several calamitous appointments, those fans can believe their team are in safe hands again.

A good win for Chelsea at Everton, but above all, let’s hope Martinez is back to full health soon.

Moyes accepted that his side had were not good enough.

He told TNT Sports: “We were a little bit unlucky with the goals. It wasn’t good defending, but it takes a couple of deflections before it gets to Neto. It makes it a relatively easy finish for him.

“The second one was a free-kick which obviously ricochets around, so I think there were parts of the game we did OK, but we didn’t offer enough to create enough, to make enough chances. I can’t think of many, so that is probably the biggest indictment.”

He had a minor gripe over a first-half tackle that was reviewed, saying, “I think the Morgan Rogers tackle on Jimmy [Garner] could have been questioned.”

However, given the good start to the season for Everton so far, he does not have too much rancour.

"Not as good as we wanted." 💬 David Moyes reflects on Everton's defeat to Chelsea 🔵 🎙️ @jules_breach | Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/qPU64VjHYC

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Xabi Alonso gives relatively positive news on Emi Martinez.

He describes the planned tests as “precautionary” and says, “as far as I know, he left the stadium conscious.”

Neto added more detail to his thoughts on the game.

On his first goal, he explained how Everton’s defensive approach allowed them to react: “We know that they came man-to man. In the second half we adjusted some stuff. We tried to get the best of the man-to-man press and we got away. We got the cross and I could finish well, so really happy.”

He credited his Portugal coach, Jorge Jesus, with his calmness in front of goal, adding: “This comes a little bit from the new coach of the national team that says when you are near to the area you need to pass to the goal, so really happy with that.”

With Chelsea now in the Champions League places, Neto was keen to keep up the momentum. He said: “It’s really important. We know it’s tough to play away, even at home there are no easy games. We came here with personality, with good intentions to win the match and really happy with the result.”

You can follow all the 3pm games here with our clockwatch.

Leading the charge for your attention is Brentford, who welcome Liverpool.

In a quick post-match interview with TNT Sports, Chelsea forward Pedro Neto says “this win is for him” after Martinez’s grim injury.

He said: “A shame for Emi but we wish him all the best … this win is for him. A clean sheet in his honour. In the second half we adjusted some stuff.”

Xabi Alonso leads the celebrations as Chelsea salute the away end! 🥳 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/AfwQAdYAmu

Everton are now in sixth place, but they might drop further. Their are five teams beneath them who would leapfrog them with a win, and Liverpool, Hull and Leeds amongst them are just a point behind.

Three points for Chelsea, who move into fourth place and keep their first Premier League clean sheet in nine months. Everton were enthusiastic, but they were ragged and then fell away once they went behind.

Chelsea, meanwhile, started loosely but tightened up, and became increasingly efficient.

However, both sets of players will likely be looking to follow up with Emi Martinez after he was forced off after a clash of heads with Jarrard Branthwaite, and was set to go to hospital. Let’s hope we get some good news soon over his health.

Quenda is on for Neto, who is likely the matchwinner.

Everton are focusing on long balls now. It’s not edifying, and so far it’s not effective either.

Chelsea’s last Premier League clean sheet was on January 17th, nine months ago.

There are nine minutes or so still to come from the added time indicated, but we may get more because of that late goal, and these two substitutions.

⬅️ Caicedo, Hato ➡️ Lavia, Palestra 🍬 0-2 ⚪️ [90] #CFC | #EVECHE https://t.co/Xq7zvjyXEB

Palmer smashes the ball into the wall from the free-kick, and the ball drops into the box.

Neto is the fastest to react, and he calmly slots the ball home off his left. Two clever finishes for the player today.

Neto fires past Pickford to double Chelsea's lead! 🔥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max 📺 https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/SOJeBP5mq0

Penders drops the ball as he tries to claim a long throw. It is worked back to Barry to head towards goal, and Penders deals with that far more calmly. Palestra and Welbeck are set to come on for Chelsea. Norgaard is the latest booking, dragging Palmer’s shirt as hard as he can. Eight yellows so far.

The free kick is about 25 yards out and well placed for Palmer, in the middle of the goal.

It’s three on one for Chelsea’s frontline. Tarkowski is the one man, holding them up as he covers both balls for Palmer. He opts for Pedro to his right, but he fires far too close to Pickford. That should have been game over, but Chelsea wasted a golden chance.

Penders races from the edge of the six-yard box to punch clear from just inside the area.

Grealish and Armstrong are replaced by Christian Norgaard - making his debut since his move from Arsenal - and Johnson.

A quick update on Martinez. The goalkeeper has been taken to hospital for further checks and treatment. That is all the detail we have for now.

Tarkowski appears to catch Rogers in the box as he turns towards goal, but the video review gives nothing.

It’s a corner on the left wing for Chelsea. Henderson takes, but it’s cleared, and Palmer’s shot from 30 yards is well struck, but wide.

Brennan Johnson will be on soon, it seems, as Moyes starts chasin’ it.

10 minutes of normal time remaining, and Everton are playing almost as if they’re holding on, but they’re behind.

Chelsea captain Reece James’ surgery could be out for a couple of months, Xabi Alonso explained.

He told the  press: “I wish him the best recovery. We won’t set timelines, but we expect him to be out for several weeks. It’s not going to be short. Whether it’s before or after Christmas then time will tell. It needs to be done properly.”

He is looking to vice captains Moises Caceido and Levi Colwill to step up in his absence, explaining: “You can be a captain without an armband, for sure. Leadership is important and that’s why we have this group, not just on matchday.”

James remains vital to Chelsea at their best, and while his minutes have been managed, it’s a huge disappointment to see him need to go under the knife once more.

In his press conference ahead of the weekend, Everton boss David Moyes was not too concerned by his relatively small squad.He said:  “Leicester City won the league with not too many players. We have not got too many players. I am not saying we’re going to win the league, but we want to try to challenge and be around the top teams.”

That might be made harder by the news that the Friedkin Group are already looking to sell the club after only a couple of years in charge. Moyes is a rare thing, a manager who keeps improving despite setbacks, and his second spell has been fairly solid so far.

Moyes is aware that Chelsea pose a threat up front, adding: “Their attacking line is incredibly exciting. I also think they have got some super defenders as well, but they are playing quite an expansive game, which on its day can lead to goals and on another day it can lead to defeats.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Everton vs Chelsea.

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend looking to harness the momentum of their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth before the international break. That Stamford Bridge masterclass ended a frustrating three-match winless streak and was built upon braces from Joao Pedro and Jordan Henderson, alongside another strike from summer signing Morgan Rogers.

Yet the true catalyst for the resurgence was the return of Moises Caicedo. Having shaken off the calf problem that hindered his early-season involvement, the midfielder anchored the side’s win. While defensive vulnerabilities persist - extending an unwanted run of league matches without a clean sheet back to January - the victory offered clear signs of progress under their head coach, Xabi Alonso.

Next up is a notoriously difficult trip to Merseyside to face Everton in Saturday’s lunchtime fixture. Historically, Everton have proven to be a formidable stumbling block for the capital club, particularly on home turf. Everton enter the weekend unbeaten in eight of their last nine home encounters against Chelsea, a stretch that has seen the Londoners fail to score on seven visits and suffer six defeats, including a chastening 3-0 reverse last term that spelt the end for Liam Rosenior.

David Moyes will demand a sharper defensive showing from his side this time around, following a frustrating 2-2 draw with Hull City where a 2-1 lead slipped away. Even so, Everton’s broader defensive record at home offers encouragement, having kept clean sheets in two of their opening three league fixtures at their base.

With both teams eager to build consistency, Saturday’s clash pits Chelsea’s newly found attacking spark against an opponent that traditionally relishes this fixture.

#1332. Scott McTominay and girlfriend Cam Reading announce pregnancy: Ex-Man United star celebrates 'precious gift' months after having heart surgery

Published: 11:18 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026

Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have announced they're expecting their first child together.

The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself.

They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino.

The couple wrote: 'The most precious gift, a lifetime of love.' McTominay, 29, and Reading have settled into life in Italy after he joined from Man United and revived his career, winning the Scudetto and earning Player of the Year honours.

It remains to be seen whether the baby will be born in Italy or back in the UK but the couple were overjoyed at sharing their happy news.

It is not exactly clear when McTominay and Reading first crossed paths but they have at least been together since the summer of 2023, when they were pictured on a boat trip in Greece.

Cam Reading and Scott McTominay shared the news that they're expecting a baby

Reading posted this picture of her bump on her Instagram page and wrote of a 'precious gift'

Reading, a director at asset management firm Fortress Capital partners, has seen her personal celebrity skyrocket in that time, zooming up from 10,000 Instagram followers to over 90,000.

According to La Repubblica, they have moved into a house by Lago Patria, a coastal lake near the suburb of Giugliano.

There, McTominay can be by the seaside quickly after popping out of his door and is only around a 20-minute drive from Napoli's training centre.

The couple regularly share photos from their new life together in Italy and McTominay is adored by fans having repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the 2024-25 season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

This season has been less straightforward for McTominay. The Scotland international underwent heart surgery after being diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health.

Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training.

But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli, scoring the winner against Torino on Saturday.

McTominay and Reading also posted this snap of the ultrasound and positive test

The midfielder scored the winner on Saturday for Napoli against Torino

He has now scored 33 goals in 92 matches across all competitions with the Partenopei and remains one of Serie A's leading lights.

The Italian press gushed over his contribution on Saturday, with Corriere dello Sport writing: 'He played with fire in his belly.

'Three shots in the opening 16 minutes; seven in total—three on target— and a decisive goal (his fourth against Torino, his favourite Serie A opponent, along with Inter), plus the charisma of a leader.'
